title: Source tax tariff basics and computed result
purpose: Ask the denomination and whether the spouse works. Combine these with the child digit and the cross-border outcome into the full Zurich tariff code (or the Liechtenstein result), which Lonio records for HR instead of HR using the calculator.

stories.title: State the denomination for the church-tax part of the tariff
stories.i_want: every employee who is subject to source tax to state whether they belong to the Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed church, or to none or another denomination
stories.so_that: the church-tax suffix (Y or N) of the Zurich tariff code can be set, and employees who are not subject to source tax are not asked about their religion
stories.priority_reason: The church-tax suffix is part of every tariff code Lonio computes (D-001); without it no tariff code can be produced, and asking non-subject employees would collect sensitive data no party needs (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination is asked only from employees subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered the residence and residence-status questions, and Lonio has determined whether the employee is subject to source tax (rule 'subject to source tax': everyone living abroad; in Switzerland only non-Swiss employees without a C permit who are not exempted by a Swiss or C-permit spouse living in Switzerland)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the source tax details
acceptance_criteria.then: the denomination question is asked, and must be answered, only if the employee is subject to source tax; employees not subject to source tax are never asked it

acceptance_criteria.title: Allowed answers for the denomination
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked the denomination question
acceptance_criteria.then: exactly two answers are possible: 'Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed' or 'None or other'; the question cannot be left empty; no more detailed denomination is collected, and the answer is recorded for HR as an input to the source tax tariff code

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination sets the church-tax suffix
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax has answered the denomination question
acceptance_criteria.then: the church-tax suffix is 'Y' for 'Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed' and 'N' for 'None or other', as in the Zurich calculator

stories.title: State whether the spouse or registered partner works, for married employees and registered partners
stories.i_want: married employees and employees in a registered partnership who are subject to source tax to state whether their spouse or partner is gainfully employed or receives replacement income
stories.so_that: the married tariff letter can be set (C if the spouse works or receives replacement income, B otherwise) without asking single, divorced, widowed or separated employees an irrelevant question
stories.priority_reason: The married tariff letter cannot be determined without this answer, and HR names it as the question the calculator adds for married employees (F-hr_transcript-09b3fe); it blocks the computed tariff code (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse employment is asked only from married employees and registered partners subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has stated their civil status and Lonio has determined whether the employee is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the source tax details
acceptance_criteria.then: the question whether the spouse or registered partner is employed or receives replacement income is asked, and must be answered, only if the employee is subject to source tax and is 'Married' or in a 'Registered partnership'; separated employees count as single for source tax and are not asked, nor are single, divorced or widowed employees

acceptance_criteria.title: Allowed answers for spouse employment
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked whether the spouse or registered partner is employed or receives replacement income
acceptance_criteria.then: the answer is 'yes' or 'no' and cannot be left empty; the question covers the spouse's or partner's employment and replacement income only (the employee's own income is always earned income and is not asked, D-006); the answer is recorded for HR as an input to the source tax tariff code

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse employment sets the married tariff letter
acceptance_criteria.given: a married employee or registered partner subject to source tax has answered the spouse employment question
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio determines the married tariff letter
acceptance_criteria.then: the letter is C if the spouse or partner is employed or receives replacement income ('yes'), and B if not ('no'), as in the Zurich calculator

stories.title: Determine the tariff letter, including the cross-border letters
stories.i_want: Lonio to determine the Zurich tariff letter for every employee subject to source tax from the answers already given (civil status, spouse employment, single-parent situation and cross-border situation)
stories.so_that: I no longer have to click through the Zurich calculator with the employee's answers to find the tariff letter
stories.priority_reason: Replacing HR's manual calculator step is a core product decision (D-001); today HR sits with the answers and clicks through the calculator for every employee (F-hr_transcript-563a9f).

acceptance_criteria.title: Base letter for married employees and registered partners
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax is 'Married' or in a 'Registered partnership' and the cross-border tariff does not apply
acceptance_criteria.then: the letter is C if the spouse or partner is employed or receives replacement income, and B otherwise

acceptance_criteria.title: Base letter for single, divorced, widowed and separated employees
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax is 'Single', 'Divorced', 'Widowed' or 'Separated' (separated counts as single for source tax) and the cross-border tariff does not apply
acceptance_criteria.then: the letter is H if at least one child counts with H (single-parent tariff), and A otherwise

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-border letters for employees living in Germany
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax lives in Germany and the cross-border tariff applies (daily return with a certificate of residence, or no daily return although a return is reasonable and not more than 60 non-return days are expected); a certificate answered 'not yet' counts as 'no'
acceptance_criteria.then: the base letter is replaced by its cross-border letter: A becomes L, B becomes M, C becomes N, H becomes P; in every other case the base letter is kept

acceptance_criteria.title: No tariff letter for employees not subject to source tax; unverified paths
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is not subject to source tax, or the employee's answers follow a calculator path that was not explored
acceptance_criteria.then: employees not subject to source tax get no tariff letter; special tariffs such as D (second job) and the replacement-income tariffs G and Q are never produced (D-006, D-009); the paths not explored in the calculator (residence block for A/B/H, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N, the full combination of paths) are compared with the calculator by a domain expert before go-live (see OQ-calculator-coverage); child answer combinations whose outcome is not yet known stay undetermined until verified (see OQ-child-paths-undetermined)

stories.title: Compute and record the source tax result for HR
stories.i_want: Lonio to compute the full Zurich source tax result for every employee subject to source tax - the tariff code made of tariff letter, child digit and church-tax suffix (e.g. C1Y, L0Y), or for Liechtenstein residents the 'in principle no source tax liability' result - and record it for HR
stories.so_that: I get the correct tariff code without clicking through the calculator myself, and I am alerted to the Liechtenstein cases that need attention
stories.priority_reason: This is the outcome of the product decision to replace HR's manual calculator step (D-001, F-hr_transcript-563a9f); HR uses the Zurich calculator for every employee today (F-hr_transcript-4e180e).

acceptance_criteria.title: Tariff code is composed of letter, child digit and church-tax suffix
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is subject to source tax and does not fall under the Liechtenstein 'in principle no source tax liability' case
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio records for HR a tariff code made of the tariff letter, followed by the number of children that count for the tariff (0 if none), followed by the church-tax suffix Y or N - the same code the Zurich calculator gives for these answers

acceptance_criteria.title: Liechtenstein result follows the calculator
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee lives in Liechtenstein (and is therefore asked the source tax questions)
acceptance_criteria.then: with daily return to Liechtenstein, or with not more than 45 expected non-return days, Lonio records 'In principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' instead of a tariff code and flags the case for HR; with more than 45 non-return days it records the normal tariff code, marked 'subject to the double taxation agreement' as the calculator does. How HR sees the flag belongs to the later HR-side spec (D-034)

acceptance_criteria.title: Result is always derived from the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: a source tax result has been recorded for an employee
acceptance_criteria.when: any answer it depends on changes (before submission by the employee, after submission by HR, e.g. a certificate of residence handed in later)
acceptance_criteria.then: the result is derived again from the latest answers and only the current result counts; the employee cannot change answers after submission (D-037). Before go-live a domain expert compares the computed codes with the calculator for the paths not explored (see OQ-calculator-coverage)

acceptance_criteria.title: Tariff code cannot be computed yet for undetermined child situations
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is subject to source tax, does not fall under the Liechtenstein 'in principle no source tax liability' case, and at least one child's answers form a combination whose outcome the calculator exploration did not show
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio records that the tariff code cannot be computed yet instead of a possibly wrong code, so the case stays visible for HR; the outcome of these combinations is to be verified by a domain expert (see OQ-child-paths-undetermined and OQ-calculator-coverage)
